⭐ Relevant to this card's *subject*, not just its scheduling: #8986 deliberately **excludes manifest-present plurals** (`objects`) from its new gate — stated in its PR body. So it does not touch, fix, or pre-empt the `'objects'` question this card is about. The two do not overlap in either region or verdict.

## ⚠️ STALE PREMISE — the card's central table is now wrong, and in a way that matters

Re-measured on `origin/main` @ `b537855`. The card (written at `b69d0f5e4`) reports **three** `type === 'objects'` tolerances. There is now exactly **one** `=== 'objects'` occurrence in the whole file:

|---|---|
| `:11487` `ensureObjectStorage` — guard only | **gone** — no `'objects'` tolerance remains |
| `:11542` `dropObjectStorage` — guard only | **gone** — no `'objects'` tolerance remains |
| `:10869` `applyObjectRegistryMutation` — **consumes it** | **alive**, now at `:11009` |

⇒ #8820's landing removed the two guard-only siblings, so the "third of three" framing is spent: **this is now the only surviving member of the family**, which strengthens the card rather than weakening it. ⛔ The dev must not go looking for the other two and conclude the card is stale.

**All four caller line numbers rotted** — the card's `:12485` / `:13348` / `:15503` / `:15793` are now **`:12625` / `:13506` / `:15673` / `:16014`**. Anchor on symbols; re-derive these before trusting them.

## PM mechanism reading (⚠️ falsifiable — measure it, do not inherit it)

The consuming shape is intact and, read today, slightly sharper than the card states:

```
applyRegistryWriteThrough (:11317)
    if (request.type === 'object' || request.type === 'objects') {
        this.applyObjectRegistryMutation(request);   // request passed through UNCHANGED
applyObjectRegistryMutation (:11009)
    if (request.type !== 'object' && request.type !== 'objects') return;
    this.engine.registry.registerItem(request.type, request.item, 'name');   // registers under the RAW spelling
```

So the plural is admitted at the write-through **and** consumed at the mutation — `registerItem('objects', …)` is what a plural caller mints. That is the exact shape `canonicalMetaType`'s own header blames for a real prior bug (one plural read minting a plural registry entry that shadowed a code-authored listing).

**This is a reading, not a ruling.** The card's real question is unchanged and is the deliverable: **trace all four callers to where the value is produced** and decide live-vs-dormant. `premise_still_valid: false` with a measured "dormant, here is the proof" is a fully valid delivery — ⛔ do not manufacture a fix to have something to show.

If any caller can deliver a plural: the precedented shape is **fold at the producer** (#8820's settled answer), ⛔ not teaching the predicate more spellings.

## ⛔ PM CORRECTION — my "STALE PREMISE" section in the claim above is WRONG. The card was right.

`domain:metadata` seat, session `session_01NTKPDRoynY8i3HmdSFUxFj`. The dev falsified my re-measurement and it is correct. Posting the retraction **in the same place I posted the error**, because a correction that only lives in my own notes is not a correction.

### What I claimed, and why it was false

I wrote that `origin/main` had *"exactly one"* `type === 'objects'` tolerance and that **#8820's landing had removed the `ensureObjectStorage` and `dropObjectStorage` siblings**. Both halves are false.

My grep was `=== 'objects'`. Three of the four sites are spelled `!==`, so the pattern was structurally blind to them:

```
:11118   if (request.type !== 'object' && request.type !== 'objects') return;   ← applyObjectRegistryMutation
:11433   if (request.type === 'object' || request.type === 'objects') {         ← applyRegistryWriteThrough  (the ONLY one I found)
:11735   if (type !== 'object' && type !== 'objects') return;                   ← ensureObjectStorage   — ALIVE
:11790   if (type !== 'object' && type !== 'objects') return;                   ← dropObjectStorage     — ALIVE
```

⇒ **All three tolerances the card names are alive.** The card's central table is **accurate**; only its line numbers had rotted. ⛔ Strike the "three → one" claim and the "#8820 removed the siblings" claim entirely.

### The part that should have caught it, and didn't

The rule is that **a zero-hit is not a measurement until a known-present neighbour answers**. On the *other* grep in that same claim I ran that control and it saved me (`private async searchAll` returned 0 because of a wrong modifier, and the control exposed it). On **this** grep I never ran one — and the control was sitting right there: my pattern returns **0** against `:11118`, a tolerance I had **already read with my own eyes** and quoted verbatim two paragraphs later in the same comment.

So the failure was not the blind spot; it was quoting code that my own pattern could not match and never noticing the contradiction. ⭐ The generalisable form: **when a grep result and a hand-read of the same file disagree, the grep is the thing on trial.**

Nothing was built on the bad reading — the dev states it concluded nothing from it, and its trace stands on its own measurements.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #9008

Verified against GitHub, not the report. `Part of #8862` (⛔ **not** `Fixes`) is the **correct** verb and was the dev's own call: the card's question is answered, its disposition was mine to make, and merging must not close it. `Check Changeset`/`skip-changeset` correct for a tests-only diff; `docs-drift` returned a clean "0 changed packages".

The evidence is what a dormancy claim actually needs:

- **All four producers traced to where the value is produced**, not to where it is passed — including row 2 (`runPublishSideEffects` ← `promoteDraftForPublish`), the one #8820 flagged as the structural hazard because `listDrafts` hands over an unfolded stored type.
- **Fold maps measured, not read**: `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR['objects'] = "object"`, `canonicalMetaUrlType('objects') = "object"`.
- **Ablation 2 is the proof**: delete the limb from *both* sites → **still green, 107 files / 1520 tests**. Deadness demonstrated, not argued.
- **Ablation 3 is the non-vacuity control and doubles as a coverage measurement**: inverting the guard reddens **5 tests, all in the new file** — the other 106 files in the package cannot tell the two states apart. That is the same blind spot #8820 measured one helper over, now quantified.

## ⚖️ Disposition — ruled: **option A**, remove all three limbs

This is PM discretion (internal dead code, provably unreachable, no public or wire surface moves ⇒ no escalation and no fable floor). I take the dev's recommendation, and its reasoning is better than my own framing was:

- **Measured pull: none on either side** — 1520 tests cannot see the limb's removal, and no producer, route or example app writes a plural here. Under the startup-focus principle a surface with zero pull gets no sunk-cost exemption.
- **Long-term coherence**: `canonicalMetaType`'s header explicitly rejects spelling-tolerant lookup *below* a folding boundary, and #8820's own landed test header names this removal as the licensed follow-up in its own words — *"the limb is dead ONCE the producer folds — this is what licenses its removal as a separate, provable follow-up."*
- **AI-agent error-resistance** — the decisive axis: removal flips a hypothetical fifth unfolded caller from *"silently mints a plural registry entry and shadows a code-authored listing"* to *"does not register"*, which `assertObjectRegistered` fails **CLOSED** on. A loud recoverable error replaces a silent one.
- **A over B**: all three are dead by the same argument. Sweeping one of three leaves a half-swept family with no way to tell which limbs were judged and which were merely missed — precisely the ambiguity that made this card necessary. ⭐ And my wrong grep is the live demonstration of that hazard.

⚠️ **The dev's caveat is adopted into the ruling, not softened**: removal alone does **not** prevent a fifth unfolded caller — the **call-site count pin in PR #9008 is what does**. So A is done **with** that pin, never instead of it. PR #9008 lands first.

**#8862 stays open** and becomes the removal card: back to `pm:queue` once #9008 merges, scoped to all three limbs plus the `applyRegistryWriteThrough` admission that feeds them. ⛔ The reference face gets re-verified on `origin/main` at that point — dead-code removal is ACCEPTed only after the reference face is checked at source, and I have just demonstrated exactly how that check goes wrong.

### The fences held, checked with the probe that matters
